newsitem.title: USA: TECO has intervenors agreement on Polk costs.
newsitem.headline: TECO has intervenors agreement on Polk costs.

text.p: Tampa Electric Co said Wednesday it has reached agreement resolving all the pending regulatory issues associated with the Polk Power Station.

The TECO Energy Inc subsidiary noted the agreement with the Florida Office Of Public Counsel and the Florida Industrial Power Users Group is subject to Florida Public Service Commission approval. It provides for full recovery of all of the expected capital costs and operation and maintenance expenses associated with the Polk Power Station. It also extends through 1999 the rate freeze currently in effect and sets additional reductions to customers' bills.
TECO spokesman Mike Mahoney noted Polk is the first commercial use of combined cycle technology integrated with coal gasification, using Texaco Inc technology.
He said the plant, now being tested, is expected to be in commercial operation next month.

The agreement calls for Tampa Electric's base rates to remain frozen at current levels through December 31, 1999, TECO said, noting this represents a one-year extension to the rate freeze agreement approved by the commission in April.

Customers will benefit from a $25 million temporary base rate reduction to be credited to bills over a 15-month period beginning October 1, 1997. This reduction will be netted against refunds which might otherwise have been made in 1999 under the existing rate freeze plan, the utility said.

The new agreement leaves intact the $25 million refund under the company's existing rate freeze plan which will be credited to customer bills over the 12 months starting October 1, 1996. It also provides for the possibility of additional refunds in the year 2000.

TECO said the agreement, which closely parallels the company's existing 1996-1998 rate freeze plan, refunds 60 percent of the revenues generated in 1999 which contribute to a return on equity above 12.00 percent to customers in 2000 along with any 1999 revenues which contribute to an ROE above 12.75 percent.
In the 12 months ended July 1996, the utility's earned rate of return on equity was 12.31 percent, Mahoney said.

The actual capital cost associated with the Polk Power Station project to be included in Tampa Electric's rate base under the agreement will not exceed one percent above the $506 million estimate presented by the utility in the prudence hearing.

Tampa Electric said it agreed to remove from its rate base the $5 million investment it has made in land at Port Manatee. A citizens' siting task force recommended using previously mined land in Polk County over the Port Manatee site as the preferred location for the new power station.
